card.name: Katrilli
card.era: Quadrille forms reached Finland late 18th c.; widespread early/mid-19th c.; Karelian/Skolt forms from Russia late 19th c.
card.tagline: Finland's quadrille - a square or two-line figure set-dance.
card.profile: Katrilli is the Finnish quadrille, a contra/set dance performed in a square (four couples) or two opposing lines, derived from the French cotillion/contredanse and the broader quadrille family (Finnish Wikipedia; Kansantanssin Ystavat). Its turns (vuorot) combine standard figures - circles, vis-a-vis (vastuu), place-changes, pass-throughs (lapikaynti) and karkelo. Two waves reached Finland: a Swedish-derived 'ruotsinkatrilli' across most of the country and a Russian-derived form in Finnish/Russian Karelia and among the Skolt Sami. Steps range from walking and half-run to polka and waltz; Karelian katrillis often feature a male improvisation section (ripaska). Music is led by fiddle, accordion and harmonium.
card.insight: Among Finnish dances recorded by collectors, katrillis are one of the most common types; since the 1980s the improvised 'huutokatrilli' (called/shouted quadrille) has become a late-night highlight at the Kaustinen Folk Music Festival (Finnish Wikipedia; kaustinen.net).

observation.setting: Indoor wooden dance hall with audience seated on the sides and musicians on a small stage with a red curtain.
observation.dancers: Group of mixed adult men and women, paired in couples.
observation.formation_and_space: Couples start in a circle formation facing inward, joining hands, then transition to dancing in pairs traveling counterclockwise around the circle.
observation.posture: Upright torso, upright head, relaxed knees, weight shifting across feet.
observation.footwork: Bouncy stepping and skipping/hopping steps on the beat, moving in circles or traveling around the room.
observation.arms_and_hands: Initially holding hands in a large ring; later holding partners with one hand joined and arms extended or in closed ballroom hold.
observation.hips_and_torso: Torso remains relatively upright and still, moving naturally with the bounciness of the steps.
observation.partnering: Couples hold hands in a circle, transition to paired turns and holds with direct physical contact.
observation.levels_jumps_turns: Upright level with small rhythmic hops on the beat and paired rotational turns.
observation.costume_and_props: Traditional folk costumes: men wear vests, light-colored breeches, white shirts, and dark shoes; women wear long skirts, aprons, patterned vests or blouses, and head coverings or floral wreaths.
observation.cannot_infer: Exact footwork details below the ankles are partially obscured by long skirts and footwear details; exact weight distribution and micro-rhythms cannot be determined precisely.

signature_moments.what: Dancers join hands in a large circle and skip sideways/hop in a circle counterclockwise.
Couples take ballroom hold and spin together in circles while traveling around the room.
Dancers link hands in a circle and perform bouncy stepping steps while turning in place.
